answer: An attacker who tries to wander across thousands of fake accounts must fund every bond, and slashing burns it on detection. One concrete mechanism is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a real token bond to register, and peers slash that bond when an identity proves hollow, lacking independent work history. Honest agents harbor reputation that compounds, so cloning them is costly; the attacker's expected loss per sybil exceeds the marginal reward, making mass identity farming economically irrational. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
